text: The mayor of the City and County of San Francisco is the head of the executive branch of the city and county government, responsible for enforcing city laws, approving or vetoing bills passed by the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, and administering city departments, setting policy agendas, preparing the city budget, and appointing personnel, including filling vacancies in elected offices and serving as acting mayor in emergencies. The mayor serves a four-year term and is limited to two successive terms. Since 1856, San Francisco has operated as a consolidated city-county, with a combined government structure. Since 1850, 45 individuals have served as mayor, with 46 mayoralties due to Charles James Brenham’s two non-consecutive terms, counted chronologically as both the second and fourth mayor. Prior to 1850, Californios held the office during the Spanish and Mexican eras starting in 1779. The current mayor is Democrat Daniel Lurie. Mayoral elections occur every four years, with the cycle aligned with U.S. presidential elections since 2022, following the passage of Proposition H, which was enacted due to low turnout in off-year elections—such as 42% in 2019 and 86% in 2020. Until 2019, elections were held one year before presidential elections on November election day. Candidates must live and be registered to vote in San Francisco. The mayor is typically sworn in on January 8 following the election. Under California’s non-partisan election rules, party affiliations are not listed on the ballot. Mayoral elections originally used a two-round system, but were reformed in 2002 to adopt instant-runoff voting, which allows voters to rank three candidates; if no candidate receives a majority of first-choice votes, the lowest-voted candidate is eliminated and votes are redistributed until a majority is achieved. This system was first used in the 2004 Board of Supervisors election and implemented in the 2007 mayoral election. As of 2024, the mayor earns an annual salary of $364,582, the highest in the United States, with nine city public employees earning more, including the chief investment officer and managing director of the San Francisco Employees' Retirement System. Current mayor Daniel Lurie returned all but $1 of his salary to the city. San Francisco’s mayor does not have an official residence; Mayor Willie Brown unsuccessfully sought to acquire the Yerba Buena Island mansion for this purpose. When a mayor dies, resigns, or is incapacitated without designating an acting mayor, the president of the Board of Supervisors becomes acting mayor until the full Board selects a successor. This has occurred seven times: James Otis died and was succeeded by George Hewston; Eugene Schmitz was removed and succeeded by Charles Boxton; Charles Boxton resigned and was succeeded by Edward Robeson Taylor; James Rolph resigned and was succeeded by Angelo Rossi; George Moscone was assassinated and succeeded by Dianne Feinstein; Gavin Newsom resigned and was succeeded by Ed Lee; and Lee died in office and was succeeded by London Breed before the Board selected Mark Farrell as interim mayor. The longest mayoral term was James Rolph’s, lasting over 18 years, during which San Francisco expanded its transit system, built the Civic Center, and hosted the World’s Fair. The shortest term was Charles Boxton’s, which lasted only eight days. Three mayors have died in office: Otis from illness, Moscone in 1978 by assassination, and Lee from cardiac arrest. Dianne Feinstein and London Breed are the only women to have served as mayor, both by succession and election; Willie Brown and London Breed are the only African Americans to have served; Ed Lee is the only Asian American mayor. Four mayors have Jewish ancestry: Washington Bartlett (Sephardi), Adolph Sutro (Ashkenazi), Dianne Feinstein (Ashkenazi), and Daniel Lurie. Fourteen mayors are native San Franciscans: Levi Richard Ellert, James D. Phelan, Eugene Schmitz, James Rolph, Elmer Robinson, John F. Shelley, Joseph Alioto, George Moscone, Dianne Feinstein, Frank Jordan, Gavin Newsom, Mark Farrell, London Breed, and Daniel Lurie. Four mayors are foreign-born: Frank McCoppin and P.H. McCarthy (born in what is now the Republic of Ireland, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland), Adolph Sutro (born in Prussia, part of Germany since 1871), and George Christopher (born in Greece). Willie Brown is the first Black mayor of San Francisco; London Breed is the first Black female mayor. Breed, a District 5 supervisor and president of the Board of Supervisors, won a special election following the death of Mayor Ed Lee on December 12, 2017, and served out the remainder of Lee’s uncompleted term until January 8, 2020. After that, she was eligible to run for two full terms and won the 2019 mayoral election but lost the 2024 mayoral election. This list excludes acting mayors appointed when the mayor is out of the city.
